Listings here have a Mission mailing address, and the real estate board groups Durieu with Mission, but Durieu is an unincorporated farming community in the Fraser Valley Regional District's Area F, in the Hatzic Valley north of Hatzic Prairie. The regional district describes the valley as including the historic settlements of Hatzic Prairie, Durieu, Miracle Valley and McConnell Creek. Property taxes are paid to the Province on the rural schedule (5% penalty after July 2, another 5% after October 31). Mission's market figures aren't Durieu figures.

items.t: This page covers the farming community of Durieu in the Hatzic Valley, north of Hatzic Prairie. Listings here show the "Durieu" area with a Mission mailing address, on streets including Sylvester Road, Stave Lake Road, Farms Road, Sward Road, Seux Road and Durieu Road. Despite the mailing address, it isn't in the City of Mission.

The regional district says almost all Area F residents live in the southwest of the Hatzic Valley, between the north shore of Hatzic Lake and the south shore of Stave Lake. The valley is reached by Stave Lake Road from Mission and by Sylvester Road from the south. Most of the inhabited area is in the Agricultural Land Reserve, with commercial and hobby farms and scattered homes.
Planning and zoning framework: FVRD official community plan and zoning bylaws govern this area (the Hatzic Valley OCP covers the inhabited valley). Confirm with the FVRD for the PID.
Flood history: the FVRD's Area F history records that a flood in 1948 broke a dyke along Hatzic Lake, the lake grew five times in size to 25 km², and the Hatzic Prairie was largely under water.
School-district coverage (SD75) and local governance are different things — SD75 serves this FVRD community even though the City of Mission does not govern it.

Health care: Mission Memorial Hospital, 7324 Hurd Street, Mission, consists of a 25-bed medical inpatient unit, a 20-bed PATH unit and a 10-bed Christine Morrison Hospice, and provides primary acute care, outpatient and inpatient services, general medicine, laboratory and diagnostic services.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Durieu

items.t: Secondary suites in Area F have a hard shape limit: the FVRD records significant limits on development options in Electoral Area F with the majority of lands in the ALR, and that secondary suites are freely permitted with no restrictions related to farm use, but must be located within the principal dwelling and could not be a separate detached structure, such as a garden suite, or a multi-unit structure for farm workers. City of Mission suite rules (registration, the $63 annual fee) do not apply here.

On ALR land: one main house of up to 500 m², plus at most one additional detached home of up to 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less or 186 m² on larger ones; a suite only if it's entirely inside the main house and local bylaws allow it. Subdividing needs Agricultural Land Commission approval, and ALR homes can't be stratified.

blocks.text: Good to know about Durieu condos

items.t: A detached garden suite doesn't count as a suite here. In Electoral Area F, a secondary suite must be inside the main home. The only way to have a detached second home is as an additional residence on ALR land (90 m² or 186 m², depending on the parcel's size), and regional district zoning must allow it too.

Most of the settled valley is farmland in the Agricultural Land Reserve. The regional district says most of the inhabited Hatzic Valley is in the ALR, with commercial and hobby farms alongside scattered homes. So for most Durieu purchases, the ALR's limits on homes and its bar on stratifying matter, not city suite or strata rules.

There is no Durieu market statistic to hide behind. No SnapStats figure is quoted for this FVRD community and no sub-area median exists record — pricing a Durieu acreage is comparable-by-comparable work on the property's own evidence, not a median lookup.
